claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 17 years old and he lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and living with you, I need to check a few more details to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (for example, school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Since Alex has left education or training but has registered with the local careers service, he may still qualify under the 20-week extension period.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the picture:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good. Now I have another important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any arrangement where Alex lives with someone else for part of the time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one more question to clarify:

**Since Alex left school and registered with the careers service, do you know approximately when he registered? Specifically, was it within the last 20 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was quite recent - just a few weeks ago actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 17 years old and lives with you full-time in the UK
- Although he has left school, he has recently registered with the local careers service
- The rules allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks for 16-17 year olds who leave education or training and register with a government-sponsored careers service
- Since Alex registered just a few weeks ago, he's well within this 20-week extension period
- No one else is claiming for Alex, and he lives with you full-time

You should be able to claim (or continue claiming) Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already made a claim, you can do so through the usual Child Benefit application process.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
